standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the hypothesis on p into reducedness of R-hat modulo p R-hat, which converts associated primes into minimal primes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Faithful flatness of the completion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the end of the counted proof (lines 46128-46129)
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets nonzerodivisibility of an element be lifted from the completion back to R.

core_obligations: Translate the hypothesis into reducedness of the completed quotient, so that an associated prime q is the same as a minimal prime over p R-hat (proof lines 46120-46123).
Identify the maximal ideal of the localisation at q with p extended there, choose x generating p in the localisation of R at p, and see that x generates that maximal ideal (proof lines 46124-46128).
Use faithful flatness of the completion to conclude that x is a nonzerodivisor in the localisation, which makes it a discrete valuation ring (proof lines 46128-46130).
proof_roadmap: Replace the associated primes of the completed quotient by minimal primes via reducedness (proof lines 46119-46123).
Exhibit a generator of the maximal ideal that is a nonzerodivisor, using faithful flatness of the completion (proof lines 46124-46131).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a Noetherian local ring R and a prime p such that R_p is a discrete valuation ring and p is analytically unramified, every localisation of the completion at an associated prime of R-hat modulo p R-hat is again a discrete valuation ring (statement lines 46106-46117). The proof does not redo the theory of analytically unramified primes: it converts the hypothesis into reducedness of the completed quotient, so that associated primes become minimal primes over the extended ideal, reads off a generator x of the maximal ideal from the corresponding generator in R_p, and uses faithful flatness of the completion to see that x is a nonzerodivisor (proof lines 46119-46131). Deciding that faithful flatness supplies the nonzerodivisor is the step that closes the argument. H2.
